subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw continue to support gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback as an explicit break-glass origin policy for non-loopback Control UI deployments?
rationale: Current main already rejects arbitrary mismatched browser origins and audits exposed fallback as critical, but the fallback still weakens DNS-rebinding defenses by design and removing it could break operator deployments that rely on Host-header based access.

options.title: Keep audited break-glass fallback
options.body: Keep the current explicit flag, critical audit, startup warning, and docs, and close this only if maintainers accept that operator-controlled risk.

options.title: Remove the fallback
options.body: Delete the flag and require explicit allowedOrigins for non-loopback Control UI deployments, with release notes and upgrade guidance for affected operators.

options.title: Replace with narrower proof
options.body: Keep compatibility only behind an additional CSRF/device/token or constrained-origin mechanism and add upgrade tests before changing defaults.

recommendation.title: Keep audited break-glass fallback
recommendation.body: Keep the current explicit flag, critical audit, startup warning, and docs, and close this only if maintainers accept that operator-controlled risk.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc merged the closest recent gateway HTTP origin hardening and is the strongest history signal for this boundary.
